later_events.mechanism: reference_substitution_by_later_order: EO 10461 (June 17, 1953), held APP transcription, section 2(a) amends each reference in any prior order to the Director of Defense Mobilization to refer to the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization provided for in Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1953, and section 2(b) names EO 10433 among the orders to which that applies; section 6 makes it effective when the first Director under the Plan enters upon office, a date no held source gives, so the signing date June 17, 1953 is recorded only as the order's date. It changes who is named and does not revoke or shorten EO 10433.

research_rationale:
EO 10433 (February 4, 1953, Dwight D. Eisenhower; 18 FR 761), read in full in the held Federal Register text, amends every reference to the Defense Production Administrator and Administration in prior orders to refer to the Director of Defense Mobilization and the Office of Defense Mobilization (section 1(a)), transfers the Administration's records, property, personnel and funds to the Office (1(b)), revokes section 1 of EO 10200 while continuing the boards, committees and positions established under it (1(c)), rewrites section 401(a) of EO 10161 so that the Director of Defense Mobilization is ex officio the Economic Stabilization Administrator (section 2) and keeps other actions in effect (section 3). The order has no stated term. EO 10480 (August 14, 1953), held APP transcription, lists it in section 607 among orders "superseded or revoked". That is the first end for every row.

savings.reason: The transfer of records, property, personnel and funds in section 1(b) and the revocation of section 1 of EO 10200 in section 1(c) were completed acts; they are not reversed when EO 10433 ends. EO 10480 section 606 keeps in effect actions relating to functions it affects. Whether the continued boards and committees of EO 10200 survived under EO 10480 is not shown by the held text; that is a disclosed qualification.
